subject.title: Feature request: Local plugin scanner CLI for pre-publish validation

question: Should `clawhub package validate` become the stable public pre-publish security scanner, and which findings should promise parity with hosted ClawScan?
rationale: Current main deliberately separates local Plugin Inspector validation from submitted-artifact ClawScan, and changing that boundary affects security expectations, untrusted-code execution, rule versioning, and CI compatibility.

options.title: Expand advisory validation
options.body: Add deterministic static security checks to `package validate` while documenting hosted ClawScan as authoritative for publish decisions.

options.title: Promise scanner parity
options.body: Package the hosted scanner stack for local use with explicit rule-version pinning, isolation, and compatibility guarantees.

options.title: Keep current boundary
options.body: Retain local metadata and compatibility validation while improving remediation after the hosted scan runs.

recommendation.title: Expand advisory validation
recommendation.body: Add deterministic static security checks to `package validate` while documenting hosted ClawScan as authoritative for publish decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the current local dry-run boundary and explicitly scoped public support out, making them the strongest history-based routing candidate.
